Configuring lychee checks

Source: vignettes/lychee-options.Rmd
lychee-options.Rmd
library(rambutan)

rambutan’s defaults are usually fine for a quick check, but real projects tend to need at least one exception: a flaky internal host, a longer timeout for a slow API, or a status code that should count as “fine, actually”. This vignette covers the two ways to configure check_url(), check_urls(), check_paths(), and check_package(), and how they combine.

Two ways to configure

  • lychee_options() – pass an options object to any check_*() call. Good for one-off overrides, or for settings that differ between calls.
  • lychee.toml – drop a lychee.toml file in your working directory and every check_*() call picks it up automatically. Good for settings you want to share between an interactive session and CI, or for a project that already has a lychee.toml for the ‘lychee’ CLI – rambutan reads the same file, using the same field names.

Every argument to lychee_options() shares its name with the matching lychee.toml field, so the two are interchangeable once you know one of them.

Precedence

When both a lychee.toml file and a lychee_options() argument set the same thing:

  • For most fields (timeout, max_retries, accept, user_agent, …), whatever you pass to lychee_options() wins over the file, and the file wins over lychee-lib’s own built-in default.
  • For exclude, include, and header, the two sources are combined rather than one replacing the other – a URL excluded by either the file or the function call is excluded.

The example below writes a lychee.toml that excludes port 9001, then calls check_urls() with an exclude for port 9002. Both URLs end up excluded, which is only possible if the file and the argument were merged rather than one overriding the other. Nothing here touches the network – 9001/9002 on localhost are never listened on, so the check is deterministic and offline-safe.

project_dir <- withr::local_tempdir()
writeLines('exclude = ["9001"]', file.path(project_dir, "lychee.toml"))

withr::with_dir(project_dir, {
  check_urls(
    c("http://localhost:9001/aaa", "http://localhost:9002/bbb"),
    options = lychee_options(exclude = "9002")
  )
})
#>                         url is_success code
#> 1 http://localhost:9001/aaa      FALSE   NA
#> 2 http://localhost:9002/bbb      FALSE   NA
#>                                details
#> 1 This is due to your 'exclude' values
#> 2 This is due to your 'exclude' values

Both rows report is_success = FALSE with details explaining they were excluded – not that the connection failed – confirming the pattern from the file and the pattern from lychee_options() were both applied.

Configuring per call with lychee_options() 

check_urls(
  c(
    "https://www.r-project.org",
    "https://api.example.com/flaky-endpoint"
  ),
  options = lychee_options(
    timeout = 30,
    max_retries = 5,
    accept = c("200..=204", "429"),
    user_agent = "rambutan-ci"
  )
)

lychee_options() validates its arguments as it builds the object, so a typo like passing a vector where a single value is expected fails immediately rather than surfacing a confusing error from inside lychee:

lychee_options(timeout = c(10, 20))
#> Error in `lychee_options()`:
#> ! `timeout` must be a single number or NULL

Sharing settings with a lychee.toml file

If you already run the lychee CLI in CI (for example via lycheeverse/lychee-action), rambutan can read the exact same lychee.toml – no duplication needed:

lychee_toml <- '
exclude = ["\\\\.local", "^https://internal\\\\."]
timeout = 20
max_retries = 3
accept = ["200..=204", "429"]

[header]
Accept = "text/html"
'
writeLines(lychee_toml, file.path(project_dir, "lychee.toml"))

With this file in the working directory, a plain call now runs with those settings applied automatically – no options argument needed:

withr::with_dir(project_dir, {
  check_urls(c("http://svc.local", "https://internal.example.com"))
})
#>                            url is_success code
#> 1             http://svc.local      FALSE   NA
#> 2 https://internal.example.com      FALSE   NA
#>                                details
#> 1 This is due to your 'exclude' values
#> 2 This is due to your 'exclude' values

In your own project this looks even simpler, since you likely won’t need to juggle a temporary working directory:

check_package(".")

Options rambutan doesn’t (yet) support are simply ignored rather than causing an error, so a lychee.toml written for the full lychee CLI keeps working here even if it sets something rambutan doesn’t expose.

Reference

See ?lychee_options for the full list of supported fields – exclude/include, timeout, max_redirects, max_retries, retry_wait_time, user_agent, method, accept, the exclude_all_private/exclude_private/exclude_link_local/ exclude_loopback IP filters, require_https, include_mail, and header.
